slides.say: For every number t, diamond of t is equal to t squared. In the choices, x is zero or more. Which of the following is not always true?

Look at the choices. The diamond appears in every choice, two or three times. That means a lot of calculating. So here's a tip for the exam. When the operation sits in every choice, skip the question, solve the rest of the section, and come back to it at the end, because it can eat a lot of time. [short pause] We'll solve it two ways, with algebra, and then by plugging in a number.

[short pause] With algebra, we write what the diamond does on each side. The diamond squares whatever goes in. Choice number one. On the left, six x goes in, so we get six x, squared. That's six squared times x squared, thirty-six x squared. On the right, thirty-six times x squared. Both sides are equal for every x, so this one is always true, and it's out.
Choice number two. Diamond of root x is root x, squared, which is x. So the left side is x times x, which is x squared. The right side is diamond of x, x squared too. Always true, so it's out.

Choice number three. On the left, five x, squared, is twenty-five x squared. On the right, five times x squared is only five x squared. These are equal only when x is zero. For any other x, they're different. So this one is not always true, and choice number three is our answer.
at: and choice number three is our answer

slides.say: In the exam you'd circle it and move on. But choice number four teaches something useful. x minus seven and seven minus x are opposites, and opposites have the same square. So the two sides are always equal.

[pause] Now let's plug in a number. It's usually faster, because we don't open anything. x is one, the simplest number allowed. Choice number one. Diamond of six is thirty-six, and thirty-six times diamond of one is thirty-six times one, thirty-six. Equal. Choice number two. Diamond of one is one, and one times one is one. Diamond of one is one too. Equal.
at: Diamond of one is one too

slides.say: Choice number three. Diamond of five is twenty-five, but five times diamond of one is five times one, which is five. Twenty-five is not five. Choice number four. One minus seven is negative six, and seven minus one is six. Negative six squared and six squared are both thirty-six. Equal.

One example where a choice fails proves it's not always true. Only one choice can be the answer, and choice number three is the one that broke. Choice number three. [pause] Okay. I'll see you in the next question.
